angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 7,259,630 km at 80.13 pc = 1.21 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 26634: distance 80.128 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.029), at which the luminosity and radius hold (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 80.128 +/- 2.324 pc; Gaia DR3 parallax 11.4008 +/- 0.4452 mas (same row, RUWE 2.12), 25.6 standard errors, is not used
radiusSource: Radius 10.435 solar radii from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 26634: radius 10.435 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 411.675 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.874) and temperature (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 7,259,630 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. No mass is measured, so GM is 0, the records' unpublished value. Temperature 8054 +/- 3803 K from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 26634: effective temperature 8054 +/- 3803 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.31) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 26634: effective temperature 8054 +/- 3803 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.31) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433)
spectralTypeSource: SIMBAD, * alf Col: spectral type B9Ve (2006MNRAS.371..252L)
objectTypeSource: SIMBAD, * alf Col: main object type Be*, Be Star
projectedRotationSpeedSource: SIMBAD, * alf Col: projected rotation speed 195 km/s, the measurement SIMBAD prefers (2005yCat.3244....0G)
rotationPeriodMeasuredSource: Measured in this project from the TESS mission's own 2-minute light curves of sectors 5, 6, 32, 33, 98 and 107 (packages/telescope-cli/src/archives/tess/reduce.mts), by the method and criteria of Holcomb et al. (2022, ApJ 936, 138): 1.1 d, the light swinging by 0.04% as the star turns

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's measured spectrum (Burnashev (1985), Abastumani Astrophys. Obs. Bull. 59, 83; VizieR III/126, part2 record 69 (BS 1956)) (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.

surfaceGravitySource: log g 3.5 from 2018MNRAS.474.5287A; the 3 published values span log g 3.2 to 3.5, across which the limb law changes by at most 0.0% of the centre brightness (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2018MNRAS.474.5287A)
